stories.title: LA County sues State Farm for false advertising, stiffing wildfire victims
stories.text: Hailee Steinfeld in State Farm’s 2026 Super Bowl commercial Jake from State Farm, call your office. The company kicked off 2026 with a splashy Super Bowl commercial featuring two popular comedic actors, Danny McBride and Keegan-Michael Key, as insurance agents for a fictional State Farm competitor, Halfway There Insurance. The duo riffs on the Bon Jovi classic, Livin’ on a Prayer: There is damage to your home on this block We won’t make things right cuz filing a claim is tough No luck Whoa, we’re halfway there Whoa, you’re living on a prayer State Farm described the ad, which also includes a cameo by Jon Bon Jovi himself, as “a humorous parody that encourages viewers to not settle for coverage that makes you feel ‘halfway there.’” The ad “exaggerates potential common consumer frustrations with their insurance experiences, from confusing terms to impersonal corporate environments.” No expense was spared. The full ad debuted during the most widely watched broadcast of the year and was extended through March Madness. In 2025, State Farm spent $1.139 billion on advertising . stories.title: AOC: Democrats Shouldn’t Be Afraid To Use Presidential Power
stories.text: While condemning President Donald Trump ’s “record level of lawbreaking,” Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) told The Lever today that Democrats shouldn’t be afraid to use the newly expanded powers of the Oval Office to deliver their agenda should they win the presidency in 2028. “I do not believe in [the idea that] when Republicans are in charge, they dramatically expand executive power to pursue their own agenda, and then when Democrats are in charge, they falsely handcuff themselves and say, ‘We can't do anything,’” she said. “So I do think that there is an extent to which we must use the tools of the office that have been provided for and allowed.” She added, “We need to put a lot of guardrails back in place, and also we cannot allow that to hamper us from doing everything in our power to guarantee healthcare in America, raise wages, strengthen unions, and more.” Ocasio-Cortez’s comments on executive power come as speculation grows around whether she’ll announce a run for the Democratic presidential nomination next year. stories.title: What the Hasan Piker Freakout Is Really About
stories.text: Abdul El-Sayed with Hasan Piker Fundraising fell off a cliff this summer. Not accepting a dime in corporate ad money allows me to be genuinely independent; but it also means I’m ENTIRELY dependent on readers like you to survive. Litigating Piker’s comments about Israel not representing all Jews is, in fact, a fool’s errand. Understand the media frenzy for what it is: a DEFCON 1-level war against Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, by a Party establishment frantically hitting the panic button to reestablish its control. But since El-Sayed is the nominee for Senate — a chamber the Party also wants to control — it has to go after him indirectly, through proxies like Piker. I could go into Hasan’s comments and the context being withheld in the mainstream depictions (see his comments in their entirety here ), but what’s the point? If you want to know why Piker is a diversionary skirmish compared to the full war, just listen to former Biden White House spokesperson turned MS NOW host Jen Psaki lament the real issue here: that the Party leadership is losing the ability to select its own candidates. stories.title: Leaked Files Reveal Uganda’s Secret Drone Deals with Israel
stories.text: This is essential to our mission: to report on what matters most, beholden only to the truth. In that spirit, we made a commitment to ensure that our journalism is free for everyone, not locked behind a paywall. But that means we rely on the voluntary support of our community of readers. Uganda’s parliament last month authorized an unprecedented deployment of Ugandan soldiers to Gaza as part of an international force proposed by President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace. “The President of the Republic of Uganda is ready to deploy in the Gaza Strip,” Defense Minister Kiryowa Kiwanuka told lawmakers in a parliamentary debate about the deployment, saying a formal status-of-forces agreement would be negotiated after parliamentary approval. The vote on the measure came after Israel said that troops from “friendly countries” could participate in the mission. The Ugandan government has so far offered no clear public explanation for why it volunteered for the mission, what role its soldiers would play, or what Kampala expects in return. stories.title: Israel’s Restrictions on Engine Oil Threaten Gaza’s Ability to Generate Electricity
stories.text: The workshop of Abna Fares Abu Zayed, a private generator company in the area of Al-Zawaida in the central Gaza Strip. August 2026. Photo courtesy of Mohanad El-Hemrawi. NUSEIRAT REFUGEE CAMP, Gaza Strip—In the corner of a ground-floor room with a door that no longer closes, Emad Mahdi sits cutting nylon sheets into squares. Beside him is a pile of barbecue skewers, the kind sold for grilling meat. He glues the nylon to the skewers, ties them with thread, and leans each finished kite against the wall. Mahdi, 60, is known in the camp as Abu Haidar. A photograph on the wall shows him holding a clothes iron, standing beside a friend. Both men are smiling. A crack from a nearby airstrike runs across the concrete wall. Abu Haidar now makes kites for the children of Al-Nuseirat, although this was not his trade. The room where he now cuts and glues was once his dry cleaning shop, where he washed and pressed clothes for 37 years. stories.title: Before Deadly Floods, Trump Diverted Emergency Responders To Beautify D.C.
stories.text: Before this week’s Grand Canyon flash floods left at least two people dead and stranded 80 in the national park, President Donald Trump’s Interior Department moved 300 specialized emergency response personnel from across the country to the capital — not to prepare for disaster, but to help with his pet “beautification” projects. The 300 specialized personnel are part of the National Park Service’s Incident Management Team and usually are first responders to natural disasters such as floods and other emergencies, CNN reported on Aug. 25. Pulled from the Incident Management Team’s 10 regional offices, the Interior Department has used the staffers to help renovate the East Potomac golf course and assist in the controversial Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool upgrades. The emergency responders are reporting directly to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, which is “highly unusual,” an employee told CNN. Create a FREE account, or log in.
